declarations.name: fixedMask_splitSample_cond_map
declarations.independentReviewText:
**T07, HEAD L128–140, proof L141–274 — actual positive-mask joint conditional map.** The local P is the original finite Pi, whose probability instance follows from the coordinate probability instances. The local coordinate event D is C on B and C-complement outside B, using the same frozen classical membership decision as `fixedMaskEvent`. The coordinate law ρ is `cond μ (D i)`. The local `hFiniteCond` covers **every** V: if μ V=0, restriction is proved zero by measurable-set extensionality and monotonicity of `W ∩ V`; its scalar normalization is then the zero finite measure. Otherwise `cond_isProbabilityMeasure` applies because μ is finite, so the normalization is finite. This local fact supplies finite, hence sigma-finite and s-finite, coordinate measures even at zero-mass endpoints; it introduces no hypothesis.

The evaluations are measurable, each has marginal μ by `measurePreserving_eval`, and they are jointly independent under P by the product-coordinate API. The public `indep_cond_joint_map_eq_pi` is then applied to **the full evaluation family** and the whole D-event. Its joint map is the identity original vector, and its conditioning event is definitionally the original mixed mask, so `hFull` is an actual complete-coordinate conditional Pi identity. It is not obtained by multiplying separately known marginals.

The source next constructs `eNotA : Fin card(Bᶜ) ≃ {i // i ∉ B}` by explicit complement conversions and proves both inverse laws. The measurable equivalence uS restricts the same original function to predicate and negated-predicate indices. Its measure-preserving law sends `Pi ρ` to the corresponding subtype product. The ρ-families simplify to the **same** νG and νH by fixed membership. uB and uA use `piCongrLeft` with eB.symm and eNotA.symm: the API maps source-subtype-indexed functions to target-Fin-indexed functions, and these inverse index equivalences give exactly the requested source and target. Both reindexings preserve their finite Pi laws. Their product and composition therefore preserve the full joint law. The `hFun` proof checks every component and every j against the exact `piCongrLeft_apply_apply` direction, then reduces to actual evaluation of x at eB j or eA j. Thus the composed map is the frozen split map, with no reordering ambiguity. Rewriting `hFull` finishes the actual conditional joint identity. Only full-mask nonzero is assumed; separate coordinate or block positivity is never added.

declarations.name: fixedMask_splitSample_restrict_map
declarations.independentReviewText: **T08, HEAD L275–287, proof L288–316 — all-mask weighted restriction.** The branch `P E=0` comes first. It proves `P.restrict E=0` on arbitrary measurable V from `V ∩ E ⊆ E`; both sides of the weighted map identity then vanish. It does not cancel the zero weight or infer an unweighted product law from it. In the other branch, P is probability, hence `P E ≠ top`. The only cancellation is `P E * (P E)⁻¹=1` using the explicit nonzero and finite proofs. Consequently the actual restriction equals its mass times the genuine conditional restriction. `Measure.map_smul` is justified by the measurable split, and T07 supplies the normalized joint law. The target is exactly the frozen weight `P E`, not an independently postulated binomial probability.

Finite-index products PB and PA are finite, hence satisfy both s-finiteness requirements of the pinned symmetric product-event formula. Applying `prod_apply_symm hS` gives `(PB.prod PA) S = ∫ a, PB {b | (b,a) ∈ S} dPA`; this is the required anomaly-outer/background-inner order. The equality T08 is evaluated on S. The measurable split and hS justify `map_apply` and `restrict_apply`; scalar evaluation gives multiplication by P E. The only final set rearrangement is commutativity of intersection. This theorem has no mask-positivity premise and remains zero-safe even when its product factors have zero total mass.

declarations.name: fixedMask_original_ae_background_sections
declarations.independentReviewText: **T11, HEAD L400–414, proof L415–464 — positive-mask iterated a.e. transfer.** As in T09, the local normalized laws and both finite products are proved finite without new assumptions. The first move from restriction-a.e. to cond-a.e. is the **forward** scalar-measure lemma `ae_smul_measure`; it is valid for any scalar and uses no scalar cancellation. The Q-after-join event is measurable by T04 and hQ. T01 turns the original predicate into its join-after-split version for source-a.e. x. The forward direction of the exact pinned `ae_map_iff` then transports it to the actual split pushforward. T07 rewrites that pushforward to PB.prod PA using the explicit full-mask nonzero premise. Product-a.e. yields background-a.e./anomaly-a.e. sections, and the measurable-predicate `ae_ae_comm` law reverses their order. Its measurability premise is exactly hQjoin and its two s-finiteness premises follow from the explicit finite products. The final statement remains anomaly-a.e., then background-a.e. No step upgrades either quantifier to all values or cancels a zero weighted measure.
